body:
It would be interesting to dig down into exactly why you are seeing what you are seeing and whether it is an rclone problem or an ACD problem.

It certainly takes longer to list big folders and rclone has to list the folder before transferring.

I could believe that the uploading a file into a directory with 50k files might take an extra few seconds as amazon has to check the directory for duplicates before uploading the file.  Is that what you are seeing?

It might be this change on rclone's side which is making the difference df1092ef33416e562ea22050640c94f38fa2df0f which checks for duplicates before uploading.

How long is the pause before each upload with a big directory do you think (assuming you are seeing that).

I would guess you are uploading lots of small files - is that the case?

I'll start with a little bit of background.  I'm currently writing a little .net c# cli program that wraps rclone and only uses rclone as an upload/download engine and only really a single file at a time.  My program takes a file of any size, breaks it into 100MB chunks, names those chunks with a guid and a sequence number (GUID_NNNN), encrypts the chunks client side, and tracks the mapping of the real path\filename to guid in a local sqlite database.  Then I use rclone to upload the chunks to a remote acd path something like remote:rcCloudStreamer.  Since I basically flatten the structure on the remote side and every file is guaranteed unique (guids) I don't ever change the remote path.  Everything just gets dumped into a single remote folder.  I'm up to 48,000 of these chunks all in a single amazon cloud drive folder.  A blank folder takes maybe 5 min to upload a 1.5GB file (broken down to 100mb chunks) but now it takes 2 hrs in my populated folder.  I was getting ready to release my application as open source to github until I noticed this issue.  I can generate some verbose logs if you think that would help.  Here are some regular logs that I have right now.  FYI, I'm on gigapower so I have around 900/900 so It's not my internet.

Here are some logs of a few of the 100MB chunks getting uploaded using rclone (windows 10 x64)

example command line call I'm using:
c:\apps\rclone\rclone.exe copy "d:\chunks\4572fe4d83404d868870797fffcfe69d_0032" "remote:rcCloudStreamer"

I know I'm  probably quite the fringe case but I'm thinking about working around this issue by creating sequential remote sub folders maybe every 10,000 files or so or whatever the threshold should be.  But if this is something that can be fixed in rclone (maybe even a blind upload switch or overwrite if exists switch?) that would be even better. 

On the flip side my program will then download the chunks (using rclone), decrypt them, piece the chunks back together in the correct order, and rename it back to the proper name.  I have upload/download folder watchers for complete automation, kodi integration, you can start watching the file if it's a media file after the first chunk is downloaded and decrypted and it can append chunks to the final file while you stream the media.  Anyways, just trying to give back to the open source community.  I love rclone and really made what I'm trying to do possible so thanks.

I did a test uploading 50,000 files (using the default transfers 4).  That took 3h47m31 so on average 3.6 files per second.

The first 1000 files were uploaded at 3.73 files / second, the last 1000 at 3.66 so no real difference there.

However I see what is the problem with your log...

rclone takes 22 seconds listing the remote directory before transferring a 100 MB chunk when there are 50k files in the remote directory.

This is as noted in #8 

Now that I've  put df1092e in, I could stop copy traversing the remote file system at all.  This would have several advantages in your case.  I'll put a `--no-traverse` flag in as an experiment and I'll post a beta here.
Yes, My use case is exactly #8, copy one file at a time with rclone into an acd folder with many files.  Sounds like --no-traverse is exactly what I need.  Thanks.

Here is a beta with the `--no-traverse` flag - let me know what you thin!

http://pub.rclone.org/v1.30-11-g22ab4e4%CE%B2/
Just tested it, and it's working great.  Thanks!
